svg.title: Standard dopamine RL model
svg.text: Standard dopamine RL model: TD actor-critic
State value: expected future reward from state $s$
Critic, stored in ventral striatum（腹侧纹状体）
Action preference: how much the agent likes $a$ in $s$
Actor, stored in dorsal striatum（背侧纹状体）
Environment returns reward and next state
Reward prediction error, sent as phasic dopamine
burst if better than expected, dip if worse
Critic: move $V(s_t)$ toward the target $r_t + \gamma V(s_{t+1})$
Actor: if $\delta_t>0$, choose $a_t$ more often in $s_t$

g.text: Left hemisphere（左半球）, seen from the left
VTA / SNc（中脑多巴胺神经元）
Dopamine carries $\delta_t$ to both critic and actor
$a_t$ goes from dorsal striatum to motor cortex via the thalamus（丘脑）

svg.text: corticostriatal（皮层-纹状体）: synapses from cortex onto striatum
plasticity（可塑性）: synapses changing their strength
The brain has no table for $V(s)$. A striatal neuron computes it from its cortical inputs:
firing of cortical neuron $i$ in state $s$, i.e. the presynaptic（突触前）input
strength of synapse $i$: this is what is learned
Step 5 then becomes a local rule that each synapse can apply by itself:
A synapse changes only if its input was active ($x_i>0$) AND dopamine reports a surprise ($\delta_t \neq 0$).
Two factors: presynaptic activity $\times$ dopamine. The actor's rule adds a third, postsynaptic factor:
only synapses onto the striatal neurons of the chosen action $a_t$ change (pre $\times$ post $\times$ dopamine).
